utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. We hope to be continuing with the evidence of Mr. Nikcevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OGRIZOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my name is Ozren Ogrizovic. I am the case manager in Mr. Sreten Lukic's team. Mr. Ivetic is actually in the building, unfortunately he may be about ten minutes late for the start of the trial. I can only offer my apologies on his behalf. He was sick throughout the day yesterday. He just got in touch with me several minutes ago to let me know that he was in the building and on his way to the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is Mr. Lukic not available?

utterances.speaker: MR. OGRIZOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He will be arriving for our next witness in about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Was there no communication earlier about the possibility that Mr. Ivetic would not be here?

utterances.speaker: MR. OGRIZOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not have information to that effect. The last thing I heard from Mr. Ivetic was that he would be here on time; however, he called me a couple of minutes ago telling me that he was about to enter the building and would make the courtroom in about ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there anything you wish to say to us, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I apologise for my tardiness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You don't think we deserve an explanation?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I apologise. I've been ill the past few days and it's been harder for me to get here in the morning. And then unfortunately I was down in courtroom I waiting for the door to be opened until I found out that we were in courtroom III. So I would have been here a little bit -- couple minutes earlier apart from that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Nikcevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your cross-examination by Mr. Hannis will continue in a moment. I have to remind you that the solemn declaration you gave right at the beginning of the evidence that you would speak the truth, that continues to apply to your evidence until it's completed. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Nikcevic. Yesterday you told us about the OPGs, and you mentioned that the OPG that you were in numbered about ten men and you said together with Klina and Istok. Does that mean that the OPG that you were in included some men from Klina and Istok as well as some of you from Pec?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And who issued you your task or your commands? Was it somebody from Pec or from Klina or from Istok? Who was in overall command of your OPG?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would receive our tasks at the outset from the squad commander who was from Istok, and I really can't remember his name. He was a warrant officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you know from who he received orders and directions? Who was his boss?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The company commander, Krsto Djuricic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you know from whom Djuricic received orders and directions, who was over him?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander, and I really don't know who the commander was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say the commander and you don't know who that was, you don't know his name or you don't know the position he held or both?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know his name, but he was the detachment commander. I didn't know then and I don't know now. I never asked around.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: When you say "detachment commander," do you mean PJP detachment commander?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably so. Based on the system that was in place the detachment commander exercised command over the detachment, the platoon commander exercised command over the platoon, the company commander exercised command over the company, and the commander exercised command over everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yesterday you mentioned some information about call-signs. You said that when the platoon commander, Djukic, got killed the call-sign Grom was the one that you no longer used. When did Commander Djukic get killed, approximately?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Djukic was killed during the action at Streoc, I think sometime in mid-1998 but I can't be more specific. Probably sometime late in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. In that answer you went on to say then the entire group of the 1st and 5th Platoon took over the call-sign Munja. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were both the 1st and 5th Platoons from Pec?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did you two operate together or separately?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I belonged to the 1st Platoon. Whenever there was an action, we were always together.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And you mentioned Vidomir Salipur, was he in one of those platoons?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the outset he was the commander of the 5th Platoon. After Djukic was killed, he was appointed commander of the 1st Platoon. As for the chief of the Pec SUP, the chief of the police, Dragan Kerseljevic, he gave them special call-signs, one was Munja, lightning. Since he was there for support and the commander of the 1st Platoon Djukic was given the call-sign Grom, thunder-bolt.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: After Djukic was killed, Salipur took over the 1st Platoon and then who took over the 5th Platoon?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You mentioned yesterday an individual named Nebojsa Minic. During the time that he was with you, what platoon was he in?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 5th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I want to mention some other names and ask you if you know who they are; and if so, tell us what unit or organization they belonged to. Did you know Miljan Kaljevic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what group was he in?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st Platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What about Sreko Popovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zarko Popovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Srecko --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Srecko Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Pardon my pronunciation.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Srecko Popovic was a member of the 5th Platoon. I don't know for what reason, but he was replaced the same time as Minic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did he sometimes go by the nickname Bordus?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, at least not that I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And Miljan Kaljevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can intervene for the transcript before it goes too far up, at line 17, page 5, he was moved out at the same time as Minic rather than replaced, "maknut" was the Serbian word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you ever know Miljan Kaljevic to go by the nickname Rambo? Did you know him to use the nickname Rambo?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How about Sladisa Kastratovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is familiar. He was also from the 5th Platoon, and he was moved out the same time as Minic and Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, when you say they were moved out, what do you mean exactly?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were no longer members of the PJP, of the Pec SUP. I never again saw them in uniform in Pec.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And when approximately was it that they were moved out?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I think sometime in September 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you know why they were moved out?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Minic had smashed up a kiosk in Uska Street, that's what we were told. As for those others, probably there had been a check by the sector chief and the officials in charge of vetting persons who were police officers or military reservists; and after this, they were moved out from us. Be that as it may, I'm not familiar with the procedure because that wasn't my business. This is just a comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you never saw any official document regarding their removal, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: As far as you know, there weren't any criminal proceedings taken against any of them?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not that I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Are you aware that there were allegations that those three, among others, were alleged to have been involved in a massacre of civilians in Cuska village just east of Pec on or about the 14th of May, 1999?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object just to the relevance of this. It's beyond the scope. The gentleman has testified that his knowledge of Minic was that -- and the others was that they left the Pec SUP in September of 1998. If we're talking about an event in 1999 [Realtime transcript read in error "1998"], that's about as relevant for our purposes as something happening in 2003 with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, he's from Pec, he's in the area, there's evidence of a massacre of civilians in May 1999. The fact that these gentlemen may have left his group in August of 1998 doesn't mean he might not know about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a moment. The issue here is the witness's knowledge of events affecting the individuals mentioned and the circumstances in which they came to be no longer members of the PJP. Their conduct thereafter may indeed be relevant in assessing the likelihood that the witness's account of what they did or at least what one of them did is accurate, so we will allow you to proceed with this line, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One more thing then, Your Honour, the transcript says if we're talking about an event in 1998 at line 6, obviously that should be 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you again, are you aware that these -- Mr. Minic, Popovic, and Kaljevic are alleged to have been involved in an alleged massacre of civilians in Cuska village just east of Pec in May of 1999. Did you not hear about that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Late 1998 Kaljevic left the police and left the Pec area, since he was originally from Montenegro. He was a SUP official in Pec. It would have been impossible for him to be in the Pec area. As for those two, as I said before, I never saw them again since they left the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall where you were on the 14th of May, 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May 1999, I think I was at home following the injury that I had sustained near Stari Trg in Mitrovica. I was bedridden.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: When were you injured near Stari Trg?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 28th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And how long were you out of action due to that injury?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until early June or sometime into June. The departure from Pec, that's when I rejoined the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You told us about some of those radio call-signs. In the units that you were in, who carried and used the radios? Was it only your platoon commander or your company commander? How many individuals had radios? First of all in 1998.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1998 each squad commander, each platoon commander, each deputy company commander, and each company commander and possibly anyone who went to an observation post or the leader of such a group would then be given a radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you ever carry one in 1998?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, what about in 1999, was it the same, each squad commander, platoon commander, deputy company commander, and company commander?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I think we got extra radio equipment. The squads had I think two radio sets each.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in 1999 did you carry one of the radios in your squad?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And who was your squad commander in 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A man from Istok, his name escapes me now really. He was only there for a short while and I only spent a short time with him therefore.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah, you told me before you forgot his name. You mentioned some of the extra training you underwent in December 1998 in connection with being in the OPG and you told us that that training was led by Goran Radosavljevic. Did you know him before this training in December 1998?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And after that training in December 1998, did you hear anything about him or know what he was doing?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2002 he was my commander in the gendarmerie.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that after you completed your OPG training you went back to your regular work at the police station in Celopek. How big was Celopek village back then, approximately?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in terms of size or the number of residents?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Both if you can tell me.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but it had some 400 houses or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And how many police worked in your police station in Celopek back in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1998, around 15; and in 1999 we were reinforced I think up to 30, 25 to 30, 20-ish.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You described for us the kind of uniforms worn by the regular police and then the PJP, and I wasn't clear on this answer. Regarding the uniforms the PJP wore you said they wore multi-coloured navy blue jackets, shirts, trousers, and boots on their feet. Multi-coloured, does that mean like the camouflage pattern?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: PJP had blue camouflage uniforms, navy blue or a grey blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And then you mentioned later that uniform changed to an olive-green-grey, that was also a camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was there a shortage of uniforms in either 1998 or 1999 for the PJP?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it existed, but our unit had both. In 1998 we used the blue one and in end 1998 and all of 1999 we used the olive-green-grey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You told us yesterday at page 45 that -- in answer to a question: "Did any members of your PJP unit wear any non-standard uniforms different from anybody else?" And you said: "No, the principle of uniformity was highly respected." Now, however, did you not see in 1998 and/or in 1999 other PJPs in the field with all kinds of different uniforms, mixed bits and pieces that didn't match and non-standard items like bandannas or headbands. You didn't see any of that in other PJP units?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A certain number of reservists in the police wore different uniforms to ours, but they did not have bandannas. We wore bandannas only -- sorry, we wore kerchiefs only around our necks, like against sweat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you never saw any PJP wearing them around their head?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the cap, yes, because that was the time when it was very hot and some of us wore them around their head against sweating.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You were asked about the wearing of ribbons, and you explained to us that you recalled two different time-periods when you did that. The first one was after Captain Perovic had been kidnapped in July, and you said: "From then onwards I know that we wore ribbons." So how long from July 1998, when you first started wearing ribbons, did you continue to wear them?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know for how long they were worn, but I believe until September, I think. I really can't tell you for sure. It's been a long time since then.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But you stopped wearing them in 1998 sometime before the OSCE mission arrived, correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And then I think you told us that the second time-period you remember wearing ribbons was in 1999. You --

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in relation to when the NATO bombing started, how long after that was it before you wore ribbons in 1999?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe he gave the exact month and time-frame yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If I can have a citation to that, Your Honour. I see it was put to him in a question, but the answer he gave was 1999. Maybe it was earlier than the section I'm looking at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I see no difficulty about asking that question, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Nikcevic, can you recall now how long after the NATO bombing was it before you started wearing ribbons again?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We wore those ribbons during the Rugova action. Now, what time it was and how long, it was not long.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Yesterday you mentioned that after the OSCE arrived you were doing your regular police work in Celopek and then you said: "Save for the incident in Racak." Were you involved in the event AT Racak around the middle of January 1999?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For the record, the same standing objection we've been making throughout this case, since Racak has been removed from the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The decision of the Chamber will be the same as it has been all along, that when it comes to issues of command and control of the forces of the authorities, then we will allow that to be explored. And at the moment it's not clear that this questioning goes beyond that. So please continue, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Nikcevic, were you involved in the action at Racak about the 15th of January, 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think I saw your name or a name like yours mentioned as someone who was injured on that occasion. Was that you?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Who was your commander on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know who my commander was. I mean, I know today but at that time I didn't know who my commander was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Today you know who your commander was at Racak, but at the time you didn't know?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm saying today I know, being on the job I am, who my commander is; but at that time I didn't know and wasn't really interested who the commander was. I was -- I only cared up to company commander but I never saw that man.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Who -- well, how did you come to go to Racak on that date?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the orders of the commanding officer, "komandir."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Whose name was?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Krsto Djuricic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And above him you don't know who was commanding or involved in the Racak event?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you and your colleagues wore ribbons on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I don't think we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what you were told about the purpose of that action?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, does this relate to command of the action or is it going to the substance of the action? Again, they keep trying to expand the scope of this Court's ruling with respect to Racak to try and bring something into the case that is not in the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think this may well go to the question of command and control, Mr. Ivetic. Let's see where it's going before we take a stance on determining the bound in this particular instance. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall what you were told about the purpose of this action at Racak?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commanding officer told us there had been an incident, that some of our colleagues were killed and wounded near Racak and that we were being sent to arrest the persons responsible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what other units were engaged with you or did you know?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were another two groups, operative pursuit groups, at least I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know where they were from?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One was local, from that area, and about the other one I really don't know anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know if there was any support provided or assistance provided by the VJ?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you know what the outcome was in terms of anyone being arrested or anyone being killed among the Albanians in Racak?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That goes beyond the bounds of what's permissible in this case, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, it relates to another topic, Your Honour. Maybe I need to ask a different question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now you told us you were asked about: "What was the KLA practice with respect to their own casualties?" And you said: "In many, many cases they carried their own wounded and dead away and didn't leave them behind," right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That's what I answered. In many cases, not in all cases, but I cannot even remember every case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall there were a number of dead bodies left behind in Racak --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, if the purpose of this is to find out how KLA bodies, if any, were handled on this occasion, that requires exploring the merits in an unacceptable way to determine who was who in this incident and that's something that's beyond the scope of the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You told us that in many, many cases they carried their own wounded and dead away. Can you give me two or three examples where that happened by date and location?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall the date and location when they carried their losses away, because we would just know by the blood-stains. And later in Krusevac village where we found a hospital - and that's one of the examples - we saw that they had some wounded and certainly some corpses there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me show you Exhibit P1596. This will be a photograph coming up on your screen in a minute. I will tell you, sir, that we've had some evidence in this case of a plan for marking or how ribbons were to be worn in the week of July 25th to July 31st, 1998, and on the 26th of July the instruction was to wear a red ribbon on the left shoulder and a white ribbon on the right shoulder. Can you tell us anything about who this group is? Are those PJP or some other police formation? What can you tell us based on the uniforms?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that those are police uniforms. I don't know anyone in this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You described the police vests that were worn. Can you point to one in this photograph that's an example of what you described for us yesterday?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you about my unit. These people are not my unit. None of those men here is wearing the combat vest that was issued to policemen at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Would you agree with me this group here is not showing the high degree of respect for uniformity that you told us you had within your unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will object to the question insofar as that we have evidence from one witness that this may not even be Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, I appreciate that when you're wearing the earphones you tend to speak perhaps more loudly than you would. If you could, when you're speaking to each other remove the earphones so that the sound does not carry across the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, your response to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we do have that schedule in Exhibit 6D667, which talks about wearing a red ribbon on the left shoulder and a white ribbon on the right shoulder. And I think from other evidence in the case there is some -- just a suggestion that these are police and that it probably is Kosovo in 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is that evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have it to hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But I recall the witness -- I thought the witness who said it was, and then he said it wasn't Kosovo based on the hill or the forest behind them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I could assist, ribbons can be worn in many, many conflicts. There are other formations that use the same uniforms that the police had in 1998 and 1999, and the witness was the Prosecution witness K90 that said this was not Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: These are all issues that go to weight and they may be very substantial in this instance, but this is evidence that we do not want to lose sight of by excluding it at this stage. We will reserve the objection that's been taken and allow you to ask the question, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think my question was: Sir, you would agree with me that this group is not showing the same high degree of respect for uniformity that you said you had within your unit, right? Their uniforms are all mixed and matched?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The uniform as such is not mixed and matched, but you can see on the man with a moustache that he's dirty and the vests they're wearing are mixed and matched.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Between July and October 1998, were you personally involved in any anti-terrorist actions in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were those strictly MUP actions or were they joint actions with the VJ?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In end July and August I think and all of September, we worked together with the army in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall now approximately how many different anti-terrorist actions you personally were involved in during that time-period?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember each and every action and I didn't participate in each and every action, but I did take part in many of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was it as many as ten for you personally?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe it was ten; six or seven.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall where any of them were by location, name of a village or an area?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the action towards Iglarevo, opening up the road from Pec to Pristina, the main road. And since the village was under blockade - Kijevo village that was - we performed a joint action.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also from Kuza village towards Glodjane and Jablanica, Bucani, Kotradic, Papracani, that route.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you remember now approximately when any of those took place?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the period. I cannot tell you the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Did you keep any diary or take any photos of what happened during that time-period?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. It's possible that I have -- at least I had two or three photographs from all of 1998 and 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You told us that before each and every action you were told very clearly to treat civilians in keeping with the highest professional standards, and the same applied to any wounded persons and anyone arrested. Can you recall now, what was your understanding of the FRY laws about treatment of civilians and wounded persons, including terrorists or KLA? Do you recall specifically what those requirements were or what you were told?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just like before the war, the same applied throughout the war and the same applies today. I treat another the way I would expect to be treated by someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, yesterday Mr. Ivetic showed you Exhibit 6D614, and you went to a number of incidents that you had some personal knowledge of. I want to ask you a couple of questions about some of those. One of them related to Radmilo Boskovic which said between July and September 1998 several times members of the KLA carried out terrorist attacks on homes and property of hers. As I recall, the entry said no on-site investigation was carried out because of security concerns and a criminal complaint was filed against unknown perpetrators. Does that mean between July and September 1998 you - and I mean you guys in the police - weren't able to stop these crimes were catch the people doing it?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. During a period of two months this Ljubo Baranska zone of theirs was established, there were no police or military there. After that, broader actions were undertaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You mentioned rapid deployment check-points were placed so that when persons would move away from crime scenes we could put a check-point there because we did have mobile check-points. During what time-period did you have these mobile check-points?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly when, during what period, but I remember Iglarevo, however I forgot the person's name. In any case they came to his family house, he is a Siptar, he killed one person and took another two to the police --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I just wanted the time-period. If you don't know, I'll have to move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was trying to explain that. That was during that period, and perhaps you can see that in the criminal reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I can't. Maybe Mr. Ivetic can raise that with you on re-direct exam after I'm finished. I would like to show you a photograph --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, what I have here is from Exhibit P438, which is the book "Under Orders" not in evidence, but there's a photograph that I would like to show this witness. The version that is in e-court is in black and white. I have a colour photograph that we've made and given an exhibit number, and it's P3111 and I would like to use that because I think it's more useful. I've advised the Defence yesterday that I was going to use this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you saying that from some other copy of the book "Under Orders" you've managed to take a colour photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, this is the identical photograph that's in the book, but in e-court I think we have a black-and-white version of the book and not a colour version of the book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Any problem with this, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Apart from it being in "Under Orders," I don't have the providence of the photograph that "Under Orders" had to get it. I don't have the exhibit in front of me to see if they have a item, but we've been using photographs throughout this case, so I don't see that as being a strong objection on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Nikcevic, we're going to show you a photograph here in a second. Can you recognise any of the people in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in the middle of the back row, that's Salipur, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In the middle of the back row, yes, with the rifle in his left hand held up, correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us any of the other people in the photograph, on the back row far right, in the blue camouflage uniform, who's that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one with the light machine-gun or the one without? The one to the left or --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: On the back right, that's Nebojsa Minic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the last guy on the back row on the left, who is that, do you know?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Miljan Kaljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: On the back row or the front row?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The row below, the one with a radio device.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the weapon, correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And he's wearing a headband?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you know who the third individual was on the back row standing on the left with his arm up on the KLA emblem? Do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is familiar, but I'll need some time to remember his name. I will eventually.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And any of the other guys on the front row, do you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one in civilian clothes was a journalist. Next to him is Goran Radosavljevic, and I believe the other one is Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall Martinovic's first name?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We called him Mico.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know where the journalist was from or what agency he was with?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you have any idea when this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: One moment. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was going to say if he's not in the photograph I don't see how he can know without speculating but...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think we should hear what answer he can give us, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You can go ahead, Mr. Nikcevic.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this photograph was taken in Glodjane. We discussed this and I was looking at the photograph. This was their line-up to have the photograph taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And when you say "we discussed this" and you were looking at the photograph, who is "we" that discussed this?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was looking at the photograph trying to recognise people, for example, Miljan and Salipur. I was being shown this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: When? You mean just now or some prior occasion?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time. I didn't see Miljan since then, and Sala has passed away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can we resolve the first point, please, Mr. Nikcevic. You indicated that you've discussed this photograph previously. When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot recall exactly. I do remember the photograph, though. I do remember seeing it back in Pec. The photograph was taken -- well, I don't know. I can't remember. I don't remember the photograph as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's just resolve this now. You've obviously discussed it with someone before. Tell us first of all when that was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was towards the end of 1998. We were looking at photographs, and this one I remembered in particular because Goran was in it. That was the reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Who were you discussing it with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was discussing it with Kaljevic and Salipur. They each had one of this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And when was the event in Glodjane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was in 1998 during the same period when -- well, I don't know what date exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You cannot help us with a rough indication of when it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Approximately August, August or September. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't know if you can see on your photograph, but it appears to be at least some of these guys are wearing one red ribbon on their left shoulder. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one can see the red ribbon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Exhibit 6D667, which is a schedule for wearing ribbons, indicates the 29th of July, 1998, was a day in which one red ribbon was to be worn on the left shoulder. Knowing that, would you agree with me that this photo may have been taken on or about the 29th of July?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object to the speculation and also I believe Mr. Hannis is reading the exhibit wrong and I believe the exhibit is for one month, not the other months. It's possible there was another date that had the same -- but I believe it's a combination of ribbons. I don't have the exhibit in front of me to be really sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's a matter on which you can make submissions, Mr. Hannis. Mr. Nikcevic, did you say you could not recognise the person with his hand on the top of the KLA emblem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know him, he's familiar, but I cannot recall what his name was at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that a radio apparatus he's carrying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just below his right hand there's a brown bag. What's that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a bullet pouch, although some people used it to carry bandages as well or something else they needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And is that standard OPG-issued equipment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This is not standard OPG-issued equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just in case there's some misunderstanding, the witness testified that his OPG training was in December of 1998, so either whether this was in July as Mr. Hannis suggests or September, it would have been before that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're quite right. Thank you. Is it standard PJP-issued equipment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it is not. Such pouches came with the PAP semi-automatic rifle, and the reserve police forces were issued with those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In addition to the guy on the back left, isn't -- doesn't Mr. Kaljevic and Mr. Salipur, don't they both have some sort of radio or communication equipment on their vest as well?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And can you tell me what Goran Radosavljevic is wearing, is that a uniform? It doesn't look like a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it's a uniform. However, it could be. I apologise, but I have problems with my eyesight.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You told us about Nebojsa Minic and how he was removed after some breaking up of a kiosk. Do you know any more details about that event? Was anyone injured or was he just removed because of some property damage?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one was injured during that incident; however, the police patrol in civilian clothes noticed that he was breaking up the kiosk and that was it for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you agree with me that this group is not observing the uniformity principle. We've got all sorts of different mixtures of uniforms just in this small group here, don't we?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can see three members of the Pec PJP, Salipur, Miljan, and Martinovic. They are wearing the same clothes. Minic was a reservist wearing a blue uniform and we have Novakovic, the bold person, he's wearing blue clothes. It's another PJP. But this was only for the sake of the photograph. Perhaps this was no action. It might have been during a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: With regard to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, which is Novakovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The one I couldn't remember his name a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Top left. The one with his hand on the KLA insignia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You don't recall his first name, do you?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you a couple of questions, before we leave that photograph, about Salipur. You told us that he was killed around the 8th of April, 1999. I will tell you that in a -- in our exhibit P1993, it's at line -- page 7 of the English and page 5 of the B/C/S, Your Honours, in a meeting on the 11th of May, 1999, that he was spoken about by Krsto Djuricic, who is listed as the commander of the 124th Brigade company. That's your company commander, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Krsto Djuricic commanded our company. There is a tape concerning Salipur and we have an exact date there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And at this meeting at the MUP staff in Pristina on the 11th of May, he's recorded as saying: "We did not have any losses except for Salipur, who was killed while undertaking measures without our approval." Do you know what that's a reference to? What measures was Salipur taking without approval?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This is pure speculation. There's no foundation for this question. How is he supposed to know what -- unless he was at the meeting, unless he was Mr. Djuricic himself --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I resent this kind of intervention where there is a clue to the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Ivetic, this is a case where you should have asked us to invite the witness to leave. It's very difficult to know whether he be prompted by this intervention. The intervention is without foundation. He was involved in the event, was he not, himself? You --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, I don't have any information about that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If he asked that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If he asked that and then we get an answer, then there might be foundation; but I'm saying it's speculation. It's nothing more than speculation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The question is: Do you know what it's a reference to? That can be yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. Hannis. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know what the commander was referring to when he said that Salipur was undertaking measures without our approval? First of all, can you just say yes or no whether you know what that was about?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment a statement made by the commander. He knows why he said that. I do know that Salipur was killed in a vehicle, he was driving it and the vehicle was struck by a shell. He was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: At the time that happened, do you know where he was going or what he was doing?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same day fire was opened on another two or three vehicles which were coming from Montenegro. As to why he went there, I don't know, but I believe his wife was about to deliver. Once he got killed, she gave birth two days later. Since the telephone lines were down, maybe he was trying to reach Rozaje because he was on leave during that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: With regard to the photograph that's still on the screen, during the time that you were in the field in anti-terrorist actions in 1998 and during the war in 1999, did you ever see Goran Radosavljevic out in the field?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we've had that asked and answered today back at the very beginning of the session Mr. Hannis asked him that question. I don't want to be suggestive. If you want, I can track down the page reference and actually read the answers back to you. But I don't want to be accused of being suggestive to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't mind him being suggestive if I've asked the question before. I recall asking him if he knew Goran Radosavljevic before the December 1998 training and being told that he was his commander in 2002. I may have asked something that is similar to this question, but I don't think I asked this question before. I stand to be corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you have a reference, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I really don't see what harm could be done by you pursuing this further, Mr. Hannis. So you say ask the witness about seeing Radosavljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Nikcevic, did you ever see Goran Radosavljevic in the field in 1998 or 1999 during these anti-terrorist actions and during the war?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing him. By what I can see in the picture, he was there with the journalist. It is possible that he was touring the units there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic, is there re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I do have several questions in re-direct. It will be rather brief though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Nikcevic, we have to have a break at this stage. Could you again leave the courtroom with the usher and we will see you at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, your re-direct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nikcevic, I just have a few questions for you. First I see it's not on the screen anymore, if we could have P3111 on the screen, the photograph that we were looking at prior to the break. Sir, I know it's clear for the record when Mr. Hannis asked you items that are also visibly clear. Are the newspaper -- are the news journalists and Mr. Radosavljevic, do they have red ribbons anywhere on their shoulders?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, is there more than one journalist there?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe there is one. Did I misspeak and say several?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your question was "journalists," but we're talking about the one --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The one, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I must have misspoken.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Going back earlier to your testimony, you mentioned Mr. Srecko Popovic and Mr. Slavisa Kastratovic -- or Kastratovic, I apologise. Were these -- during the time-period prior to being discharged from the MUP in Pec, the SUP in Pec, were they active policemen?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just waiting for the transcript to catch up with us. And in Celopek, first of all, could you tell us precisely what type of -- what type of organized formation was that in Celopek, because it's getting several different translations in English. What was the entity in Celopek and was it under the authority of any other organized units of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police section in -- the police department in Celopek was under the jurisdiction of the police station of the Pec SUP and it employed regular policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And with respect to that element in Celopek, you testified that in 1998 there were approximately 15 policemen and that later that was increased to either 20, 25, or 30. If I could ask you, during the time-period when there were 15 police officers, how many police officers were on a duty shift at any given time? How many were on duty at the same time in the course of a regular day?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on their line of work, depending on who's in the duty service, who's on the regular beat --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask the question a different way. Were all 15 ever on duty at the same time?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Going back slightly, Mr. Ivetic, the institution or whatever at Celopek I had understood from earlier evidence was an OUP. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I could ask the witness to clarify but I don't believe so. That's why I had confusion. Because there's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's been called a station, a department, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't think the answer clarifies anything. It simply says the police section or police department in Celopek fell under the SUP at Pec.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you give us the entire hierarchy from the SUP Pec downwards to the organized entity in Celopek.

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: SUP Pec had three police departments, one in Celopek, one in Klincina and one in Ozrim, plus two branch police offices, Klina and Istok, these are OUPs and they had their own police departments. Now, where they were, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Does that clarify sufficiently for Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Not really because there's confusion in my mind about whether Klina and Istok are OUPs. I don't think they are from this, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, in the Serbian he called them OUPs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but he said that he doesn't know where they -- "where they were, I wouldn't know," suggests that these OUPs are in places he doesn't know, rather than in Klina and Istok. So it's very unclear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: He said, and I quote: "They had their own police departments. Now, where they were, I wouldn't know."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I see, so where they base their police departments is what -- yeah. So the end result is that the police department he is part of is a satellite of the SUP in Pec, which falls under no other organizational unit, it falls directly under the SUP in Pec. Is that the position that you're trying to convey?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: RADOJICA NIKCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nikcevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Nikcevic, that completes your evidence. Thank you for coming here to the Tribunal to give evidence. You may now leave the courtroom with the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you leaving us now, Mr. Ivetic, or are you staying?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I was planning on leaving, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Well, I just wanted to remind you that there's only one medicine that will cure what you have, I hope you take it and recover quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I intend to, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you can speak to my countrymen about where to get the best. We will now hear from Mr. Lukic who the next witness will be.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, good morning. Our next witness is Petar Dujkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Dujkovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration to speak the truth by reading aloud the document now being shown to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You will now be examined by Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Dujkovic.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DUJKOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I kindly ask my friend Eugene O'Sullivan to move a bit so I can see the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dujkovic --

utterances.speaker: PETAR DUJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- first of all I have to explain something to the Court regarding your written statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the witness statement of this witness there is a paragraph 23, and we have the wrong number of the exhibit inside. So to avoid the hassle we would like to remove that paragraph from his written statement, that's paragraph number 23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Take it as deleted from the statement, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dujkovic, you have seen that written statement that you signed?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DUJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I deleted paragraph 23, as we agreed, because it contained a mistake. Regarding other circumstances described in this written statement if I asked you about them again would you give the same answers as in the written statement?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DUJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hereby tender as 6D1499, which is the written statement of Mr. Petar Dujkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you have any problem with that, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. We shall admit the statement. Just give me a moment, though, Mr. Lukic, would you, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: One of the deficiencies of the electronic system, and in my opinion there are very few of them, but one is that we cannot make alterations to documents to reflect a deletion. So to resolve the question you need to substitute a redacted version of 6D1499. Now, as soon as you've done it, you should let us know. You don't need to make a filing, just tell us it's been done and we'll confirm that it's substituted for the original. And that reminds me, I should earlier have dealt with your fourth application to amend the 65 ter statement, to which there is no objection, and that application is granted. So please continue, Mr. Lukic, on the basis we shall admit the statement and you can then substitute the redacted version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After these procedural matters we can now proceed with your testimony. Mr. Dujkovic, would you kindly introduce yourself and tell us about your career.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DUJKOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Petar Dujkovic. I was born on the 12th July 1952 in a place called Gornja Brijesnica in Bosnia-Herzegovina, near Lukavac and near Tuzla. All my life I worked with the police. In 1971 I graduated from secondary police school and started to work, and later on the job I completed the higher police school and got a law degree in 1980. During that time and later I was engaged in various jobs with the police, starting as a policeman, later in more senior positions. I spent the most time working with the border police, and in 2005, if I'm not mistaken, I retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At any time in your career did you control the administration for border affairs?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DUJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, among other things, I worked at the administration of the border police, whose full name is administration for foreign nationals and border affairs. I was first assistant head of the administration; then assistant of one of the sections, the section for border affairs; and later I was assistant head -- sorry, deputy head of the administration. And in the absence of the chief, I managed the administration several years on my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, could you slowly this time repeat the full name of your administration because not all of it is in the record.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DUJKOVIC
utterances.text: It was the administration of border police, foreign nationals, and administrative affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Until what time were you at the head of the administration? You don't have to give us the date, just tell us who took over from you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DUJKOVIC
utterances.text: I was at the head of the administration until June or July 1999, when General Sreten Lukic took over, whereas I continued for another year, slightly less than a year, as his deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you a member of the collegium of ministers -- sorry, the minister of internal affairs from 1997 until July 1998 -- 1999?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DUJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was a member of the collegium.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who were the other members?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DUJKOVIC
utterances.text: Assistants of the minister, chiefs and heads of all organizational units or administrations at the seat of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before July 1999 was Sreten Lukic member of the collegium of the minister of the interior?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DUJKOVIC
utterances.text: He couldn't have been because he didn't work at the seat of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now could you tell us to the best of your recollection who was the minister and who were his assistants.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DUJKOVIC
utterances.text: The minister was Mr. Vlajko Stojiljkovic, and his assistants were General Vlastimir Djordjevic and General Rade Markovic. At the same time these two were at the head of the public security and state security administrations respectively. Another assistant was General Stojan Misic and yet another was General Zekovic. The others were chiefs of administrations, while General Obrad Stevanovic was a member of the collegium in his capacity of assistant minister and he was at the head of the police administration. Other people who attended were General Dragan Ilic, chief of the crime police; Dragisa Dinic, also a general, chief of traffic police; I attended as deputy head of administration for border police, foreign nationals, and administrative affairs. And I'm trying to remember --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This will do. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I need some guidance from you. We have a 6D1305 which is internal rules of Ministry of Internal Affairs, it's not translated but it's actually updated version in force at that time. The Prosecution was using P1072, but it was from 1994 and it's not the exact rules that were in force at that time. They are similar but not the same, so I would rather use one that is accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Subject to getting a translation, we have no objections to using this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think that makes sense. So you should use the 1996 one. I hope it's not going to cause a great deal of difficulty that it has not been translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Small changes, actually, and it can even be followed in P1072 but there are some differences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, before you move on to that can we just be clear about the ministerial set-up. There isn't a diagram somewhere, is there?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: On the assistant ministers and chiefs of sections or --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll try to find it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just let me ask just a couple of questions of the witness before you proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Dujkovic, was there a deputy minister?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time there was no deputy minister.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Has there on other occasions or at other times been a deputy minister of the interior?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In the previous period there was one, and as far as I know later when the whole staff changed there was again a deputy minister but not at the moment we are discussing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is the difference between the role of a deputy minister and the role of an assistant minister of the interior?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the difference could be is that the deputy minister is able to stand in for the minister in every way in discharging any function which is part of his job if the minister is absent for whatever reason, and the deputy minister can carry out any task he is entrusted with without being limited by the organization of the organ that he's heading, whereas assistant ministers were each in charge of one area and they could hardly take over another area. One, for instance, assistant minister was in charge of public security, the other was in state security and these were not interchangeable. Most of the other assistant ministers mostly came under public security and each of them had their own line of work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There even appears to be a situation where one assistant minister might be directly answerable to a different assistant minister. For example, the relationship between Djordjevic and Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that was possible because at the same time he was also chief of public security administration. He was at the same time assistant minister and chief of the public security administration, whereas Obrad Stevanovic was leading one unit which was part of that administration -- part of that sector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So both have the status of assistant minister?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How does that work in practice if they disagree with each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't say that because I never had occasion to witness such a situation, and in my line of work generally I had very little to do with the area of Obrad Stevanovic. I had my own assistant, if I can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Have you ever held the title of assistant minister?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've given us I think so far the names of five assistant ministers. Were there actually more than that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that was all. I think I've given you all the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what were the particular responsibilities of Misic and Zekovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Misic at the time was responsible for the work of the border police administration of foreign nationals, which is where I worked, and he was also in the fire prevention police. And there may have been some sort of a communications administration that was under him or something like that. As for General Zekovic, he was in charge of logistics. For example, the -- I'm not sure what it was called, joint affairs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And were both of them responsible to Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they both answered to Djordjevic because their organizational units were part of the sector and they as assistants had direct links to the minister but they probably had certain responsibilities under Djordjevic as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You can see why we would be assisted by some sort of chart, Mr. Lukic, if you have the opportunity to provide that. Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are recorded as saying: "I had my own assistant, if I can put it that way."

utterances.speaker: PETAR DUJKOVIC
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What did you mean, the person who was your assistant, what did you mean the assistant minister under whom you were working?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DUJKOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise for this inaccuracy. What I had in mind was the assistant who was above me who was my superior, but that's what we called him colloquially, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please repeat again who this was.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DUJKOVIC
utterances.text: General Misic was the assistant minister, he was in charge of the work of my administration, he was my superior, he was also an assistant to the minister. He wasn't my assistant, but he was in charge of my area and that's why I used the expression.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Right. That was just by way of clarifying. Thank you. Further for the sake of clarity, in addition to Rade Markovic, who was assistant minister and sector head for state security, what about the remaining assistants, the remaining three, Stevanovic, Zekovic, and Misic; were they not, in fact, subordinated to General Vlastimir Djordjevic who was chief of public security?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DUJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we please now have - and you can find that in your binder - 6D1305. We see that on our screens now. Perhaps we could have P1072, the English version, displayed at the same time. I'm not sure if the technology is working properly. Can we actually do that? All right. I see it. What sort of a document is this, sir?

utterances.speaker: PETAR DUJKOVIC
utterances.text: These are rules establishing the internal organization of the Ministry of the Interior. This was passed on the 31st of December, 1997, and this is the final version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need Article 13 in both languages. In the Serbian we're looking at page 8. [In English] We need paragraph 13, I believe it's page 8 -- actually, it's page, yeah, 10 and I think in English in the other document it's page 12 or 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dujkovic, we are facing a certain amount of trouble with our technology, and I wasn't specific enough about the page numbers, I'm afraid. According to these rules that were passed in December 1997 or based on these rules, you see the names of all the different administrations there. Can you try to remember who headed each and every one of these to the best of your recollection.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DUJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Article 13 shows all the organizational units at ministry headquarters. Number 1, crime police administration headed by General Dragan Ilic, chief; police administration headed by General Obrad Stevanovic, who was also assistant minister; traffic police administration, General Dragisa Dinic; operations centre, Colonel Milivoj Markovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Slow down, please, just a little.

utterances.speaker: PETAR DUJKOVIC
